title: Scaffold: a new project has no wired place for permission sets or datasets, and os generate has no type for them
body:
epic:#26676#1 · zhuangjianguo · session_cdb7a717def74e719988f089fbaa18ff

From a real-user walkthrough of the development flow, filed on the maintainer's word: 「第一组：会卡住人或误导人，立卡」 (2026-11-04). Measured on `main` `987ff33b88` unless a line says otherwise. Test project scaffolded with `create-objectstack@18.3.0`.

## What a customer sees

A developer scaffolds a project. An app that real users sign in to needs permission sets. The generated project has no `src/security`, the config has no key for it, and `os g` cannot make one. Datasets for a dashboard are the same. Both work once wired by hand, which is what this walkthrough did.

## Measured

- `packages/create-objectstack/src/templates/blank/objectstack.config.ts` imports objects, views, actions, flows, dashboards, apps, skills and picklists. It has no permissions or datasets.
- `packages/create-objectstack/src/templates/AGENTS.md:76` says these "are exactly the directories `objectstack.config.ts` wires" and tells the reader a new directory needs its barrel and its stack key. So the docs are honest, and the gap is the starting point.
- `GENERATORS` in `packages/cli/src/commands/generate.ts` has object, view, action, flow, dashboard, app, skill, picklist and more, with no permission set and no dataset.
- `templates/AGENTS.md` writes `npm run …` throughout, and the generated file keeps it in a pnpm project (7 occurrences, published 18.3.0). `npm run` still works there, so this is a small mismatch only.
- A plain dataset object needs `as const` to pass the type check (published 18.3.0).

## Expected

The scaffold ships a wired, empty `src/security` (and datasets, if the seat's reading of need holds in review), `os g` covers them, and the generated AGENTS.md names the package manager the project was created with.
